sections.h2: Where is the Pamlico County Tax Office and how do you reach it?
sections.html:
Look for it inside the Pamlico County Courthouse, 202 Main Street, Bayboro, NC 28515. Letters go to Box 538 there, and the counter is staffed weekdays from eight until five.

One office does the work of both assessor and collector here. It lists property, sets values, records ownership changes and collects current and past-due tax. The county commissioners appoint the Tax Administrator. The office email is tax.office@pamlicocounty.org, and three direct lines split the work.

  • Listing, for personal and business property: 252-745-3105
  • Collections and payment plans: 252-745-4125
  • Land Records: 252-745-3791
  • Fax: 252-745-4042

sections.h2: What dates does the Pamlico County Tax Office publish each year?
sections.html:
Its key dates list runs from January to September, and most entries repeat annually. Ownership is fixed on January 1 and bills are due September 1.

  • January 1: ownership is declared as of this date.
  • January 5: the deadline for paying with no interest.
  • January 31: listing period ends.
  • April: the Board of Equalization and Review begins hearing appeals.
  • May 31: the deadline to settle overdue tax before the newspaper ad.
  • June 1: final day for exemption and exclusion applications.
  • July: bills go out in the mail.
  • September 1: bills come due.

After a missed January date the state adds 2% starting January 6, and from February 1 interest grows by three-fourths of one percent per month or part of one.

sections.h2: When is the next Pamlico County reappraisal?
sections.html:
The office's own pages disagree, so ask. The last reappraisal took effect January 1, 2020. The About the Tax Office page names January 1, 2026 for the next, while the key dates list shows January 1, 2027. Call 252-745-3105 for the date that applies.

The county calls its schedule the Octennial Plan, after the state's eight-year limit. Values should track the market as of the last reappraisal date and are adjusted only at the next one. The assessor handles more than 17,000 real property parcels, plus business personal property, mobile homes and aircraft, and all of it must be valued by the same standard.

sections.h2: What are the Pamlico County property tax rates?
sections.html:
The county rate page lists 0.7000 for the county in 2026, against 0.645 in 2025. Town and fire district charges stack on that, which makes location decisive.

Pamlico County has 12 tax districts, and the money pays for schools, roads, police and fire protection. The county's worked example multiplies a $100,000 value by the town and fire rate per hundred dollars for a house in Bayboro in the Triangle Fire District. Call the Tax Office to confirm which rates apply to your parcel and whether the figures below are final for the year.

sections.h2: Which Pamlico County rates differ between the 2025 and 2026 columns?
sections.html:
The county column moved from 0.645 to 0.7000, and most fire districts moved up as well. Town rates mostly held still.

  • Grants/Slv. Hill Fire, as labeled: 0.08 in 2025, 0.1100 in 2026
  • Olympia Fire: 0.0760 in 2025, 0.1100 in 2026
  • Reelsboro Fire: 0.0821 in 2025, 0.1130 in 2026
  • FL / Whort Fire, as the county labels it: 0.0613 in 2025, 0.0810 in 2026
  • Goose Creek Island: 0.06 in 2025, 0.0700 in 2026
  • Bayboro and Vandemere town rates: unchanged at 0.27 and 0.23

A house on Goose Creek Island, one near Reelsboro and one in Bayboro can therefore draw very different bills from the same county value. Ask for the rate sheet that matches your district before you estimate what a buyer will carry.

sections.h2: How does a Pamlico County owner contest a value?
sections.html:
Put the request for a hearing in writing and deliver it to the board's clerk before the panel adjourns. The Tax Administrator serves as that clerk, at P.O. Box 538, Bayboro, NC 28515.

For 2026 the board began on April 8, adjourned May 12 and set the filing cutoff at 5:00 p.m. on May 11, so that window is closed. The real estate appeal form on the county's forms page is marked for a January through May window. The owner must show that the value or location was wrong or that the property was taxed in error. A taxpayer who loses at the board can take it to the Property Tax Commission in Raleigh by sending written notice within a month of the mailing date, 30 days to be exact.

sections.h2: What property tax relief does Pamlico County have forms for?
sections.html:
The forms page carries applications and instructions for the elderly or disabled exclusion, the circuit breaker deferment and the disabled veterans exemption. It also has forms for present use value, a property tax exemption and a business property exemption.

  • The state's income ceiling for the 2026 tax year is $38,800.
  • Under the elderly or disabled program, the larger of $25,000 and half the appraised value comes off the taxable amount.
  • For disabled veterans the first $45,000 of value is excluded, with no age or income test.
  • Circuit breaker owners pay at most 4.0% or 5.0% of income, based on how income compares with the ceiling, and the remainder is deferred.

Applications must reach the office by June 1 on the county's calendar. Roughly a third of residents are 65 or over, so many owners are in range. Call the Listing line to ask for forms.

sections.h2: What becomes of the tax bill when a Pamlico County house sells?
sections.html:
It follows the parcel, so closing must clear it. The yearly tax becomes a lien when property is listed, and penalties, interest and costs ride along with it.

Before picking a closing date, call Collections at 252-745-4125 for the balance. Overdue accounts get advertised after May 31. Where the county forecloses, the sale happens at the courthouse door. The seller also pays the deed stamp tax, $1 for each $500, at the deeds office ahead of recording. A closing attorney usually collects both from the proceeds.

sections.h2: How big and how old is Pamlico County, by the census?
sections.html:
This is a small, mostly owner-occupied county. Census staff count 12,758 residents in the 2025 estimate, 4.0% above the 2020 base, spread over 336.52 square miles of land.

Owners live in 82.9% of homes, and the middle value among them is $216,800. Median rent is $752. The county counts 5,456 households in 7,610 housing units. Residents 65 and over make up 34.9%. Median household income is $59,717 and 17.6% live below the poverty line. The rate page lists eight fire districts plus Goose Creek Island, so district lines weigh heavily on a bill. Building permits totaled 97 in 2025.

faqs.q: When are Pamlico County property taxes due?
faqs.a: September 1. Mailing happens in July, and January 5 is the final interest-free day on the office calendar.

faqs.q: Which number reaches the Pamlico County tax staff?
faqs.a: Call Collections at 252-745-4125 for payments and payment plans, or Listing at 252-745-3105 for personal and business property. The office is at 202 Main Street, Bayboro.

faqs.q: What is the Pamlico County tax rate?
faqs.a: The rate page shows 0.7000 for the county in 2026, with separate town and fire district figures added on top. Call the office to confirm your parcel's combination.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my Pamlico County assessment?
faqs.a: Not for 2026. The filing cutoff was 5:00 p.m. on May 11, and the board adjourned May 12. Ask the office about next year, since it lists April as the month the board opens.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for tax relief applications in Pamlico County?
faqs.a: The county calendar closes exemption and exclusion applications on June 1. Use the Listing line, 252-745-3105, for forms.
